name: Thurston County
deadline_pattern: December 24 at 5 p.m. each year for the following calendar year
typical_open: Fall, after the September LTAC meeting sets priorities
notes: 2027 cycle is open now; apply by email or mail to Ellen Massey.

presentation.pattern: LTAC reviews proposals in January after the December deadline, at the Atrium Building Room 110 with a Zoom option; no presentation requirement is published

meeting_schedule: Meets as needed; a September meeting sets priorities and the rubric, and review meetings are held in January (dates announced late December)

funding_docs.title: Lodging Tax Advisory Committee (LTAC) program page, 2027 cycle
funding_docs.summary: About $250,000 is available for 2027 tourism projects; applications are due December 24, 2026 at 5 p.m. and the scoring rubric and priorities are set at the September 24, 2026 LTAC meeting.

funding_docs.title: County Seeks Applications for 2026 Lodging Tax Funds
funding_docs.summary: Announced about $250,000 for 2026 local applicants with a December 24, 2025 deadline; the total award amount is finalized at the end of December each year.

funding_docs.title: 2027 Lodging Tax Application Form
funding_docs.summary: The county's application form for 2027 funds; contents could not be read because the site blocks automated access.

pool_note: 2027: about $250,000 is published as available to local applicants; total county lodging tax revenue and standing commitments are not published on the LTAC page.

name: Whatcom County
deadline_pattern: Early September each year for the following calendar year; Council approves in November
contact: Jake Logan, Whatcom County Executive Office, 360-778-5211
notes: Three grant types: events and festivals, tourism promotion, and capital/infrastructure; 22 projects were funded for 2026.

presentation.pattern: LTAC may ask some, all or none of the applicants for an oral presentation at its November review meeting, about two months after the deadline; applicants may attend and answer questions

meeting_schedule: Meets as needed; application review in September through November, with Council approval in November

funding_docs.title: 2026 Whatcom County Lodging Tax Applicant Guidelines
funding_docs.summary: Three application types (events and festivals, tourism promotion, capital); no stated caps, event grants generally run $1,500 to $30,000, and a 25% minimum match is a scoring criterion. LTAC may call some or all applicants to present.

funding_docs.title: Whatcom County Lodging Tax Guidelines (funding priorities)
funding_docs.summary: Ranks priorities: the destination marketing organization first, then chambers with visitor services, year-round visitor organizations, tourism infrastructure, and finally festivals and events in unincorporated areas that drive overnight stays.

funding_docs.title: LTAC 2026 Approvals (Resolution 2025-037)
funding_docs.summary: Council approved $3,532,390 on November 5, 2025: $812,000 tourism promotion, $275,500 events and festivals (12 awards), $2,384,890 capital, $60,000 admin. Largest awards were $1.8M for Birch Bay Beach Park restrooms, $256,000 Mt. Baker Chamber visitor center and $250,000 Bellingham Whatcom County Tourism.

funding_docs.title: 2026 WC LTAC Events and Festivals Grant Application
funding_docs.summary: Application form for the events and festivals category, the most common grant type and the one relevant to balloon events.

pool_note: 2026: $3,532,390 approved under Resolution 2025-037; $2,384,890 went to county park capital projects, $812,000 to chambers and the DMO for tourism promotion, $60,000 to admin, leaving $275,500 awarded across 12 outside events and festivals.

name: Skagit County
deadline_pattern: Annual cycle; LTAC reviews in October and commissioners approve allocations in late October for the following year
notes: A 2027 funding application is posted, but its due date could not be read; 2026 awards went to 34 groups for 43 projects.

presentation.pattern: LTAC holds its review meeting in October; presentation practice not published

meeting_schedule: Meets in October each year to review applications; other meetings as needed

funding_docs.title: 2027 Application for Funding (Skagit County Lodging Tax)
funding_docs.summary: The county's 2027 lodging tax application form; the due date and scoring could not be read because the county document server is blocked for this session.

funding_docs.title: Skagit County allocates lodging tax funds to 34 community groups (Skagit Valley Herald)
funding_docs.summary: Commissioners approved about $896,000 for 2026 to 34 groups for 43 projects, up about $81,000 from the prior year. Secondary source; the official award list is in the October 2025 LTAC minutes.

funding_docs.title: October 2025 LTAC Minutes
funding_docs.summary: LTAC's October 2025 review meeting with 2026 funding recommendations; contents could not be read because the county document server is blocked for this session.

funding_docs.title: Skagit County Code Chapter 3.17, Tourism Promotion Area
funding_docs.summary: Separate from the lodging tax: a $2 per room per night TPA charge on lodging with 40 or more units, spent on tourism promotion under a plan proposed by the Skagit TPA Advisory Board.

pool_note: 2026: about $896,000 was awarded to 34 outside groups for 43 projects per the Skagit Valley Herald; total county lodging tax revenue is not published on an accessible page.

name: Chelan County
deadline_pattern: Early to mid October each year for the following calendar year (Oct. 15, 2024; Oct. 10, 2025)
notes: The 2027 application now shows as closed with no date listed; event and marketing grants get 10% of the tax, and most of the rest goes to chambers and Visit Chelan County.

members.name: Stephen Maher
members.affiliation: Our Valley Our Future / Run Wenatchee

presentation.pattern: Not required; committee members may request a 10-minute presentation or schedule a short in-person interview before the October review meeting

meeting_schedule: Meets roughly monthly or as needed (2025 meetings: May 22, July 31, Oct. 23, Nov. 21, Dec. 10), some via Zoom

funding_docs.title: Chelan County Lodging Tax Framework 2026
funding_docs.summary: Adopted December 15, 2025: Visit Chelan County 27%, Lake Chelan and Leavenworth chambers 20% each, county facilities 20%, event and marketing grants 10%, Cascade Loop 3%, Cashmere, Manson and Entiat chambers 3 to 4% each; the extra 10% comes from reserves.

funding_docs.title: BOCC awards 2026 lodging tax grants
funding_docs.summary: Nearly $222,000 went to 35 tourism groups for 2026 out of 46 applications requesting nearly $780,000; the grantee list is a linked PDF titled Event and Marketing Grants.

funding_docs.title: County awards 2025 lodging tax events, marketing grants
funding_docs.summary: $252,350 to 23 agencies for 2025 from 48 applications requesting over $1 million; largest awards were $45,000 Tour de Bloom, $25,000 Washington Nordic Cup, and $20,000 each to the Leavenworth Bike Festival, Lake Chelan Wine Alliance and Leavenworth Summer Theatre.

funding_docs.title: 2026 Lodging Tax funding requests open Aug. 29; due Oct. 10
funding_docs.summary: $221,638 available for 2026; online application that cannot be saved, applicants must show their budget and how county matching funds would be used; LTAC favors projects that raise overnight stays.

funding_docs.title: November 21, 2025 LTAC Minutes
funding_docs.summary: LTAC recommended the 2026 percentage allocations (109% of collections, 9% from reserves) and moving $2.5 million from reserves to a restricted M&O fund for county-owned tourism facilities.

pool_note: 2026: nearly $222,000 awarded to 35 outside groups as event and marketing grants, which the framework sets at 10% of collections, so total collections are roughly $2.2 million (estimate); the other 90% plus 10% from reserves goes to Visit Chelan County, chambers, Cascade Loop and county facilities.

name: Grays Harbor County
deadline_pattern: September 15 at 5 p.m. (received or postmarked) each year for the following calendar year
contact: Grays Harbor Tourism, PO Box 1229, Elma, WA 98541, 800-621-9625
notes: Run by Grays Harbor Tourism with four grant types (festivals and events, hospitality and special projects, major tourism projects, and destination marketing), and email or fax applications are not accepted.

presentation.pattern: Optional applicant presentations about a week after the September 15 deadline (September 21 and 23, 2026); the county says it gives no advantage

meeting_schedule: Meets in late September to review applications; recommendations to commissioners in October

funding_docs.title: 2027 Tourism Grant Program Information Matrix
funding_docs.summary: Festival and event grants $100,000 total with a $7,500 cap; hospitality and special projects $100,000 with a $20,000 cap; major tourism projects $200,000; destination marketing $200,000. Window August 15 to September 15, 2026; LTAC review September 21 and 23; awards by end of November.

funding_docs.title: Grant Workshop Presentation (2027 cycle)
funding_docs.summary: $600,000 in annual awards funded by the 3% lodging tax; review criteria include drawing visitors from 50+ miles, a detailed marketing plan, leveraged funding and measurable outcomes. Since 2011, 60 of 87 applications were funded.

funding_docs.title: 2027 Festivals and Events Grant Application
funding_docs.summary: Application for the festivals and events category; presentations on September 21, 2026 are optional and give no advantage; mailed or hand-delivered only.

pool_note: 2027: $600,000 published across four grant categories ($100K festivals and events, $100K hospitality and special projects, $200K major tourism projects, $200K destination marketing); total 3% lodging tax revenue is not published.

name: Pacific County
notes: No public county LTAC grant program or application was found online.
pool_note: No lodging tax fund budget, award list or grant program was found, so neither figure can be stated.

name: San Juan County
deadline_pattern: Mid-September each year; awards in November and projects must finish by December 31 of the next year
notes: Applications go through an online portal, and a workshop is held in June.

presentation.pattern: LTAC reviews applications in September and October after the deadline; presentation practice not published

meeting_schedule: Reviews applications in September and October; award notices in November

funding_docs.title: Lodging Tax Annual Grant Program
funding_docs.summary: County program page with the online application portal; the 2026 cycle opened June 1 and closed September 11, 2026 with projects to be completed by December 31, 2027. Page could not be read directly for this session.

funding_docs.title: San Juan County announces 2025 Lodging Tax grants
funding_docs.summary: About $1.9 million awarded January 2, 2025: core funding to 11 entities (chambers $81,148 each, museums $67,624 each, theaters $60,862 each, County Fair $365,170, Visitors Bureau $535,000) plus 25 special projects, the largest $70,000 for fair equipment and $40,000 each for agritourism and the Community Theater.

funding_docs.title: Opening soon: Lodging Tax annual grant program (Islands Weekly)
funding_docs.summary: County notice for the 2026 cycle: portal opens June 1, info workshop June 16, applications due September 11 at 5 p.m., review in September and October, awards in November.

pool_note: 2025: about $1.9 million awarded, of which $535,000 went to the Visitors Bureau, $365,170 to the County Fair and fixed core amounts to island chambers, museums and theaters, leaving 25 special projects whose total is not published; the largest special awards were $70,000, $40,000 and $40,000.

name: Jefferson County
deadline_pattern: Annual cycle; LTAC votes on next-year funding requests in late November
notes: The county LTAC (Fund 125) reviews requests each November, but no current application page or due date was found.

presentation.pattern: LTAC votes on next-year requests at a hybrid special meeting in late November; presentation practice not published

meeting_schedule: Special meetings as needed, typically a late-November funding meeting in the commissioners' chambers with Zoom access

funding_docs.title: Jefferson County Code Chapter 3.25, Lodging Tax
funding_docs.summary: 4% countywide lodging tax; up to 50% for tourism facility operations, up to 25% for facility acquisition and development, at least 25% for tourism promotion, with a 25% operating reserve. Funds may not sponsor a specific event. Five-member LTAC chaired by a commissioner.

funding_docs.title: Jefferson County grants $800K in lodging tax (Peninsula Daily News)
funding_docs.summary: Commissioners approved almost $800,000 for 2025 through an LTAC request-for-proposal process; largest awards were $140,500 Olympic Peninsula Gateway Visitor Center, $109,500 Olympic Peninsula Tourism Commission and $91,500 Quilcene Historical Museum.

funding_docs.title: Jefferson County lodging tax committee to meet (Peninsula Daily News)
funding_docs.summary: LTAC's November 26, 2024 hybrid special meeting voted on 2025 funding requests plus a $10,000 capital contingency and $5,051 for county staff time to administer Fund 125.

pool_note: 2025: almost $800,000 awarded through the LTAC RFP, with $140,500 to the Gateway Visitor Center, $109,500 to the Olympic Peninsula Tourism Commission and $91,500 to the Quilcene museum; the remainder went mostly to visitor centers, county parks and marketing, and county code bars sponsoring a specific event, so no outside-event pool can be stated.

name: Okanogan County
deadline_pattern: Mid-August each year for the following calendar year
notes: Open to nonprofits and municipal visitor centers; marketing projects need a 50% match.

presentation.pattern: Required presentations at the LTAC meeting about six weeks after the mid-August deadline (September 25, 2026, 9 a.m.); award recommendations to the BOCC about a month later

meeting_schedule: Meets as needed; a September review meeting and an October recommendation meeting each year

funding_docs.title: 2027 Lodging Tax Funds Application Instructions
funding_docs.summary: Applications due August 14, 2026 at 5 p.m. with required presentations September 25 and recommendations to the BOCC October 23; marketing projects need a 50% match and wages are capped near 10% of the award. No total pool is stated.

funding_docs.title: Lodging Tax Advisory Committee page
funding_docs.summary: 4% lodging tax in unincorporated areas under resolutions 51-1998 and 37-1999; eligible applicants are nonprofits and municipal visitor centers promoting tourism to increase overnight stays.

funding_docs.title: Resolution 054-2020, LTAC Amending Committee Makeup
funding_docs.summary: Sets the committee structure by commissioner district with tourism industry and tax receiver seats; no funding amounts.

pool_note: No lodging tax fund budget or award list is published online; the 2027 instructions give no total pool.

name: Kittitas County
deadline_pattern: Mid-September each year for the following calendar year; oral presentations in November
typical_open: August, with applicant workshops in mid-August
notes: A consolidated committee (CLTAC) with Ellensburg and Cle Elum ranks applications, and workshop attendance counts toward the score.

presentation.pattern: Oral presentations to the CLTAC in late November, about two months after the mid-September deadline, at Ellensburg City Hall

meeting_schedule: Consolidated LTAC meets in late November for presentations and recommendations; municipal committees score beforehand

funding_docs.title: 2027 Lodging Tax Fund RFP and CLTAC Guide
funding_docs.summary: Applications due September 18, 2026; ongoing events capped at 10% of expense budget and returning applicants capped at the prior cycle's reimbursed amount; 100-point rubric covers workshop attendance, 50+ mile draw, matching funds, attributable lodging stays and more, with a 50-point minimum. Reimbursement only.

funding_docs.title: Kittitas County LTAC Bylaws (May 8, 2024)
funding_docs.summary: Governing bylaws for the consolidated committee of the county, Ellensburg, Cle Elum and Roslyn; no funding amounts.

funding_docs.title: City of Ellensburg Resolution 2023-05, 2023 Hotel/Motel Tax Fund Grants
funding_docs.summary: Shows how the consolidated process is adopted by each jurisdiction: Ellensburg's 2023 share was $53,321 across six awards, the largest $25,000 to the Kittitas Valley Event Center and $15,000 to Gallery One.

pool_note: 2026: $480,887 countywide pool (county $341,015, Ellensburg $108,259, Cle Elum $27,340, Roslyn $4,272) awarded in full to 25 outside applicants from $989,573 requested; the county's own share is $341,015, with no standing DMO contract taken off the top.
